name: Language study
description: Tools for learning a language (any language: French, German, Japanese, Arabic, ...). Keep a vocabulary list (one entry per line: term and translation separated by a tab, ";", "," or " - ", an optional example sentence, optional tags). Check lints it (duplicates, empty sides, invisible characters); Anki cards writes a file Anki imports; Frequency lists the most frequent words of a text so you learn the useful ones first (vowel marks ignored); Listen makes an audio file (term, a pause to answer, the translation) with Piper where a voice is installed, otherwise eSpeak-NG; Compare checks a recording of you reading a text against that text through Whisper and lists the words said differently or not heard. Translation of text: the Translate button. The original is never changed.

presets.label: Check the vocabulary list
presets.description: Lints a vocabulary list: a term with no translation or the reverse (error), repeats, the same text on both sides, an invisible character, a very long entry, a term with two translations (note). Problems come back as file(line).

presets.label: Anki cards (import file)
presets.description: Writes a tab-separated file for Anki (File > Import): front, back (translation and the example in italics), tags, with the header lines Anki reads. Type both in the extra arguments to add the reverse cards as well.

presets.label: Word frequency (what to learn first)
presets.description: The 200 most frequent words of a text with counts and cumulative coverage, how many words cover 80% of it, and how many appear once. Vowel marks are ignored.

presets.label: Listen: the list as audio (MP3)
presets.description: Reads the list aloud: the term, a pause to answer, then the translation. Type the languages in the extra arguments: term=fr trans=en pause=2 max=100 (pause in seconds; at most 150 entries). Piper is used where a voice is installed, otherwise eSpeak-NG.

presets.label: Compare my reading with the text (Whisper)
presets.description: Give a recording of you reading a text as the input, and in the extra arguments the text and the language: text=/path/to/expected.txt lang=en. Whisper transcribes it; the report gives the accuracy and lists the words said differently, not heard, or added. It shows what Whisper understood, not a pronunciation score.
